itinerary.cal: July through September; a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit covers the camp below Stuart Pass, with no camping within half a mile of Lake Ingalls. Parties usually spend two days with a camp near Stuart Pass.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: hike over Ingalls Pass to a camp under Stuart Pass, then climb the 8-10 pitch West Face Wall to the West Ridge and walk out.

days.title: Ingalls Pass to camp below Stuart Pass
days.objective: Reach the upper Ingalls Creek meadows
days.note: About 3 miles of switchbacks lead to Ingalls Pass, and Lake Ingalls is about a mile beyond. Camping is not allowed at the lake, so continue toward Stuart Pass and camp on durable ground in the meadows under the West Wall.

days.title: Climb Gorillas Direct and hike out
days.objective: Climb the West Face Wall and return to the car
days.note: The route climbs a splitter on the wall between Stuart Pass and Goat Pass in 8-10 pitches. Expect sustained 5.10 with 5.10+ on the first and sixth pitches, a 'Monkey Traverse' on pitch 3, and loose rock on the final traverse. From the top, continue up the West Ridge to the summit or descend the main gully with one single-rope rappel to the Stuart Pass bivy sites.

prior.notes: Mountain Project gives the route, pitches and descent but no approach or timing. WTA and Abegg cover only the shared approach as far as Lake Ingalls (about 3 mi to the pass, lake about 1 mi beyond); nothing opened covers lake to Stuart Pass. Day 1 gain/loss come from the row (4,269 ft trailhead, 6,457 ft Ingalls Pass, about 6,000 ft meadows camp). Day 2 is the row's 6,150 ft total minus day 1, and assumes a summit. Blake's Gorillas in the Mist party took about 30 h car-to-car from the north side with an unplanned West Ridge bivy, so it is not a template for this approach. The row's 24.1 km (15 mi) looks like a round trip, whereas the sibling King Kong row lists 7.2 km one-way.

itinerary.cal: Usually July through September as a long day on a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit; no camping at Lake Ingalls itself.
itinerary.totalNote: A long day: over Ingalls Pass to the lake, up slabs and talus to the North-South notch, then the short Southwest Face to the North Peak.

days.title: Lake Ingalls to the North Peak
days.objective: Climb the Southwest Face and return to the car
days.note: From Lake Ingalls, climb slabs, talus and boulders to the notch between the North and South peaks. Drop about 100 ft west to a friction slab, which is the start of the face. Plan for rappels on the way down. Parties starting before sunrise have reached the lake around 9 am and finished by headlamp.

prior.notes: No opened source describes the Southwest Face itself. The route text (friction slab about 100 ft below the notch, a class 3 gully, a couple of low-5th moves) appears only in search snippets from the Mountaineers and SummitPost, which return 403. Miles and gain are from Abegg's South Peak trip, which shares the approach to the same notch (about 11 mi, 4,200 ft); her 5.6 h solo is not a fair guide for a roped party, so hours are left null. Lemke climbed the North Peak by its south ridge, not this face.

itinerary.cal: July through September; a free self-issue Alpine Lakes Wilderness permit covers the camp below Stuart Pass, with no camping near Lake Ingalls. Plan two days with a camp near Stuart Pass.
itinerary.totalNote: Two days: hike over Ingalls Pass to camp below Stuart Pass, then climb the 8-pitch 5.12a wall and hike out.

days.title: Ingalls Pass to camp below Stuart Pass
days.objective: Reach the upper Ingalls Creek meadows
days.note: Climb about 3 miles to Ingalls Pass, pass Lake Ingalls about a mile beyond (no camping there), and continue to the meadows under the West Wall below Stuart Pass.

days.title: Climb King Kong and hike out
days.objective: Climb the West Face Wall and return to the car
days.note: The route shares its lower half with Gorillas Direct, then takes 'Fifth Avenue' (10+) to a two-bolt anchor and 'The Empire State Building', a steep 12- headwall splitter. A short 5th-class scramble gains the top of the wall. Bring extra 0.5-4 cams for the runout headwall. Descend the main West Ridge gully with one single-rope rappel to the Stuart Pass bivy sites, then retrace the approach.

prior.notes: Mountain Project covers the route and descent (900 ft, 8 pitches) but gives no approach or timing. WTA and Abegg cover the shared approach only as far as Lake Ingalls. Day 1 gain/loss come from the row's waypoints and camp (4,269 ft trailhead, 6,457 ft Ingalls Pass, about 6,000 ft camp). Miles split the row's 7.2 km (4.5 mi) one-way, which matches WTA's trailhead-to-lake distance more than the distance to Stuart Pass. Day 2 gain is unknown because no source gives the wall-base elevation. The row's Gorillas Direct sibling gives 24.1 km and 6,150 ft for the same approach.

itinerary.cal: June through September as a day climb from the Blue Lake trailhead; a Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is needed to park.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb: up the Blue Lake trail and the Beckey gully, five pitches on the southwest corner, then the Beckey Route rappels.

days.title: Beckey gully and the Sidewinder
days.objective: Climb the southwest corner and rappel the Beckey Route
days.note: Hike about 2 miles to the heather meadow, take the climbers' trail left into the talus-filled Beckey gully, and break left at the fork to the shelf below the cave feature. Wear helmets in the gully. Descend from the summit by downclimbing the slab to the end of pitch 3 of the Beckey Route, then make the chained rappels to the notch and reverse the gully.

prior.notes: Neither opened source covers Sidewinder; both describe the shared Beckey gully approach and the Beckey Route descent. Outbound gives about 5 mi round trip and about 2,000 ft to the notch, which agrees with the row's dist_km 4 (one-way). Gain uses the row's gain_ft 2,520; the row's elevations (5,380 to 7,720) give 2,340. No source times the route, so hours are null.

itinerary.cal: July to August, when the Chilliwack ford is wadeable and Easy Ridge and the Challenger Glacier are in shape. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is needed for each cross-country zone night. Plan about five days.
itinerary.totalNote: Five days: two days in over Hannegan Pass, Easy Ridge and the Challenger Glacier to a bivy under Ghost Peak, a ten-pitch climbing day, and two days back out the same way.

days.title: Hannegan Pass to Easy Ridge
days.objective: Ford the Chilliwack and camp on Easy Ridge
days.note: Go over Hannegan Pass and down to the Chilliwack, wade it near Easy Creek, and climb the steep path to the first camp where it reaches the crest of Easy Ridge. Seasonal tarns are the only water up there.

days.title: Easy Ridge to the Ghost Peak bivy
days.objective: Cross Perfect Pass and the Challenger Glacier
days.note: Traverse Easy Ridge over Easy Peak and solo exposed fourth class across the Imperfect Impasse, dropping to about 4,450 ft. Climb back to Perfect Pass, cross the Challenger Glacier, then descend and traverse snow, talus and glacier to a scrabbly bivy below Ghost Peak.

days.title: Climb the West Ridge of Phantom Peak
days.objective: Climb the ridge and descend the southeast face
days.note: Climb to the 6,100 ft saddle and scramble to a notch to rope up. Ten pitches follow, mostly 5.7+, with a 5.10 stemming cleft on pitch 6 and a 100 ft rappel into a notch after pitch 7. About 400 ft of fourth class leads to the summit pinnacle. Descend the southeast face; there is a rockfall-exposed snowfield on the way back to camp.

days.title: Back over Perfect Pass to Easy Peak
days.objective: Return to an Easy Ridge camp
days.note: Recross the Challenger Glacier to Perfect Pass, drop around the Imperfect Impasse and climb back to Easy Peak. From Perfect Pass alone this took one party a little over 6 hours.

days.title: Easy Ridge to the Hannegan trailhead
days.note: Descend to the Chilliwack ford, climb back over Hannegan Pass and walk out to the car.

prior.notes: The route and the two-day approach come from the only documented ascent (Wehrly and Larson, AAJ, July 2021). The AAJ does not split the approach between days or describe the exit. Yellowleaf's 2006 Easy Ridge/Perfect Pass trip supplies segment times on the shared approach: about 8.5 h trailhead to the Easy Ridge camp, about 6.2 h Perfect Pass back to Easy Peak, and about 9.3 h Easy Peak to the car. Yellowleaf's total is 12,720 ft for 4 days. Day 2 gain is a minimum (impasse low point ~4,450 ft to Perfect Pass ~6,300 ft), and day 4 gain is impasse to Easy Peak (6,613 ft). Day 3 uses the row's 1,916 ft. No per-day mileage is sourced beyond the AAJ's ~10 mi of trail and the 5-mile Easy Ridge.

heldFor: fewer than two sources; low confidence

itinerary.cal: June through September, once the Squire Creek crossing is manageable. No permit is needed. A one-day climb from the car.
itinerary.totalNote: One day: about 2-3 hours to the grassy saddle, a twelve-pitch slab-and-crack route that fast parties simul-climb, then the descent.

days.title: Squire Creek saddle and Skeena26
days.objective: Climb the twelve pitches above the grassy saddle
days.note: Walk the old Squire Creek roadbed, cross the creek (one party found logs just downstream where it splits), and climb the forest and two dirty gullies to the grassy saddle, about 2-3 hours. A fast party simul-climbing 2-3 pitches at a time topped out 2.5 hours after roping up. Plan the descent before committing; no source describes the standard one.

prior.notes: Only one opened source: climberkyle (2021), about 2 h car to saddle and 2.5 h on route, continuing to Buckeye and Whitehorse rather than descending. The CascadeClimbers FA reports return 403, and the search budget ran out before a second source could be found. Day gain is the row's 2,200 ft. The row's approach says about 3 h to the saddle. Climberkyle lists the grade as 5.8; the row says 5.9. Descent is unsourced.

itinerary.cal: June through September. No permit is needed. Done as a long single day from the hairpin, often after a night at the pullout.
itinerary.totalNote: A long day: 2-4 hours over Kangaroo Pass to the hidden South Face, eight runout pitches, then rappels on the north side.

days.title: Kangaroo Pass and the South Face
days.objective: Climb the South Face and rappel the north side
days.note: From the hairpin, take the faint, cairned climbers' trail across talus and through forest to Kangaroo Pass. Drop below the pass and traverse to the base of the South Face, 2-4 hours from the car in all. The rock varies, route-finding is challenging and there are R-rated sections. Descend by the standard rappels on the north side; one party found a single 60 m rap from the summit and a double 60 m rap to the notch.

prior.notes: Only Mountain Project describes this route (800 ft, 8 pitches, Grade III, 5.8 R, approach 2-4 h, no descent info). The 2008 blog report covers the shared hairpin to Kangaroo Pass approach and the north-side rappels, but its route is unnamed. Day gain is the row's 2,400 ft, which matches the row's 5,160 ft trailhead and 7,572 ft summit. Row says 7 pitches; MP says 8. Previous notes record MP's area page giving 7,238 ft for the summit (not re-opened). No hours or mileage are sourced.

itinerary.cal: July into October, after the Barrier crest melts out. A North Cascades National Park wilderness permit is required for the cross-country camp on the Chopping Block ridge. Usually done in three days, or as part of a longer Southern Pickets trip.
itinerary.totalNote: Three days: carry from Goodell Creek up the Barrier to the Chopping Block ridge camp, climb and rappel the four-pitch NE Ridge, and descend out.

days.title: Goodell Creek to Chopping Block ridge camp
days.objective: Carry to the ridge camp near 6,400 ft
days.note: Old roadbed up Goodell Creek, a log crossing of Terror Creek, then a climbers' path up the Barrier crest to the camp above Crescent Creek Basin. One party starting at 3 am arrived well before noon.

days.title: Climb the Northeast Ridge
days.objective: Climb the ridge and rappel back to its base
days.note: Walk and scramble southwest from camp to the foot of the ridge. Some of it is exposed 3rd class, and the lower ridge is mossy 3rd class. Climb the four pitches to the summit, then rappel the route; one party used a single rope.

days.title: Descend the Barrier to Goodell Creek
days.note: Down the Barrier crest on a faint path to about 3,600 ft, then a steep, brushy descent to the Terror Creek log and the Goodell Creek path. About 7 hours.

prior.notes: The camp, approach and walk-out come from Abegg (who descended the NE Ridge by single-rope rappels but did not climb it) and the NWHikers 2020 report. The pitch count, the 5.5 grade and the rappel descent come from the row. Search snippets, not opened (CascadeClimbers 403), describe the route as 5 pitches, 5.5, Grade II on the Mountaineers page, mossy 3rd class low down, and under an hour camp to summit simul-climbing. Gain and loss are derived from Abegg's elevations (600 / 6,400 / 6,819 ft).

itinerary.cal: June through September, once the Squire Creek ford is manageable. No permit is needed. A long single day from the car.
itinerary.totalNote: One long day: about 3 hours to the grassy saddle, roughly another hour of scrambling and traversing west past Skeena26 to the far western wall, then five pitches.

days.title: Squire Creek to the far western wall
days.note: From the saddle, go left past the base of Skeena26 and scramble about 100 m of class 4 ramps to a shelf. Cross a deep gully, where a two-bolt anchor serves for a hand line or short rappel, then follow a cairned track west over talus to the far western wall. Plan the descent before committing; no source describes it.

prior.notes: OpenBeta confirms only the grade (5.8) and the 2017 FA (Enger, Lewis, Daubert); its description is empty. Climberkyle covers the shared approach to the grassy saddle (about 2 h). The traverse beyond comes from the row's own approach text. Day gain is the row's 2,200 ft. No source gives the descent, distance or total hours.
